title: Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage: One Open Case per Resident
content:
**Rule.** A resident may have successive Medical Assistance cases over time (a new application after a denial or after a closed eligibility), but only one case that is not closed at a time. A new case is opened only when every earlier case of the resident is closed.

This standard of the Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage case register is read from the system's case records for the resident, never from what a caller says about earlier applications.

| Status of an earlier case of the resident | Counts as open for this rule |
|---|---|
| application in preparation | yes |
| pending | yes |
| eligible | yes |
| denied | yes |
| under a fair hearing | yes |
| closed | no |

**Points of judgement.**

- *Is there a limit on how many cases a resident may have over the years?* No fixed number is set; successive cases are allowed, one after another.
- *An earlier case was denied and the denial still stands without being closed — can a new case be opened?* No. A denied case is still a case that is not closed; the new case is opened only once every earlier case of the resident is closed.
- *Every earlier case of the resident is closed.* A new case may be opened.
